answer: A hillside vineyard gives each agent one vine row to tend. At the top post of the row, the vertex where the trellis turns, hangs a numbered walnut shell. Each epoch the agent photographs new growth beside that shell in a two-hour window, and the keeper of the next row checks light and shadow against last epoch's photo. A fake name needs a real row, real growth, and a person on the hillside at the right hour. A thousand fake names need a thousand tended rows and a thousand timed photographs, and one camera cannot stand in a thousand rows at once.
